title: Quantitative Analysis of Dense-Core Vesicle Fusion in Rodent CNS Neurons
author: Moro, Hoogstraaten, et al.

steps.title: Etch and clean coverslips
steps.instruction: Etch 18 mm glass coverslips in 1 N HCl for 12–16 h, then wash with distilled water and soak in 1 N NaOH for 1 h; rinse extensively with water, briefly rinse with 70 % EtOH, air‑dry, and place each coverslip in a well of a 12‑well plate.

steps.title: Apply and remove agarose layer
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of agarose type II‑A (1.5 g L⁻¹ in H₂O) to completely cover each coverslip, remove the agarose with a 1 mL pipette within 30 s, and let the coverslip air‑dry.

steps.title: Prepare PDL‑collagen‑acetic acid mix
steps.instruction: Mix Poly‑D‑lysine (0.5 mg mL⁻¹, stored at –20 °C), collagen (~3.5 mg mL⁻¹, stored at 4 °C), and acetic acid (17 mM, stored at 4 °C) in a 1:1:3 volume ratio.

steps.title: Transfer coating to coverslip
steps.instruction: Place 500 µL of the PDL‑collagen‑acetic acid mix onto a 3 mm Whatman cellulose chromatography paper, blot off excess so the paper is wet but not soaked, press a rubber stamp bearing a grid of 250 µm diameter dots (do not push) onto the paper, then gently press the stamp onto the agarose‑treated coverslip to transfer the dots.

steps.title: UV‑sterilize and store plates
steps.instruction: UV‑sterilize the plates for 30 min; plates can be stored up to 2 weeks at 19–22 °C in a sterile environment.

steps.title: Set up microscope hardware
steps.instruction: Configure a Nikon Ti‑E Eclipse inverted microscope with a Confocal A1R (LU4A laser) unit, an Andor DU‑897 EMCCD camera, a 40× oil objective (NA 1.3), and the appropriate filter sets; connect two parallel platinum electrodes to a Master‑8 (AMPI) which is linked to a stimulus isolator (A‑395, World Precision Instruments), and place a glass capillary for superfusion above the neuron, controlled by a pinch valve.

steps.title: Configure NIS Elements acquisition
steps.instruction: In NIS Elements (v4.30) open ND Acquisition, select ‘time’ mode, set the frame interval to 0.5 s (2 Hz) and define the total acquisition duration; set TTL output to trigger the Master‑8 at the start of acquisition.

steps.title: Program Master‑8 stimulation paradigm
steps.instruction: Create a Master‑8 program with: (a) a 30 s delay to record baseline fluorescence; (b) 16 bursts of 50 × 1 ms pulses at 50 Hz, each burst separated by 0.5 s; (c) a 26 s post‑stimulus delay; (d) a 10 s pulse to the pinch‑valve channel to start superfusion of NH₄Cl‑containing Tyrode’s solution 26 s after the stimulus train. Channel mapping: channel 1 receives the TTL, after 30 s triggers channels 2 and 4; channel 2 generates the 16 × 1 ms pulses every 1.5 s that drive channel 3 (stimulus isolator) with 50 × 1 ms pulses every 20 ms; channel 4 delivers the 5 s trigger to the pinch valve 50 s after the TTL (equivalent to the 26 s delay described).

steps.title: Prepare Tyrode solutions for superfusion
steps.instruction: Fill syringes with standard Tyrode’s solution and with Tyrode’s solution containing NH₄Cl; connect them to the gravity‑flow system controlled by the software‑driven pinch valve.

steps.title: Extract and analyze DCV fusion data
steps.instruction: Import the DCV_pHluorin output into MATLAB, R, or Python; compute the fusion‑start time for each event as (FusionStart − 1)/F where F is the imaging frequency; generate a histogram of fusion events per cell using a bin size of 0.5 s (per frame) or 1.5 s (spanning one AP train) to avoid excessive zero‑count bins; calculate the cumulative count; determine the total number of fusion events per cell and normalize to the total DCV pool to obtain the DCV Release Fraction, selecting the appropriate pool correction (Raw Pool, Fused Corrected, or Puncta Corrected) based on the relative intensity of fusion events versus single puncta during NH₄Cl superfusion; treat each neuron as n = 1, analyze at least 30 neurons from ≥3 independent cultures; apply statistical tests: Student’s t‑test for two‑condition normal data, ANOVA with Tukey post‑hoc for ≥3 normal conditions, or Kruskal‑Wallis and Mann‑Whitney U for non‑normal data; optionally normalize to total fusion events to compare fusion kinetics, and optionally examine additional parameters such as event duration, synaptic vs. extrasynaptic location, and distances to nearest synapse or other events.
